title: The answer is in the question
prompt: Which access method is recommended for remote CLI management? SSH is the correct answer to this question.
leaked_cue: The answer 'SSH' is stated directly inside the prompt itself.
clean_version: Which access method is recommended for remote CLI management?
explanation: Embedding the answer in the prompt turns the question into a reading exercise. The clean version states the question and nothing else — the learner must recall or reason to answer.

title: Steered by adjectives
prompt: Obviously the secure option is SSH — which protocol should you choose for remote management? (Hint: pick the secure one.)
leaked_cue: The words 'obviously' and 'secure' steer the learner toward SSH before the question is even asked.
clean_version: Which protocol should you choose for remote management?
explanation: Leading wording leaks the answer through loaded adjectives and a redundant hint. The clean version stays neutral so the learner evaluates the options instead of following the wording.

title: Spelled out in the hint
prompt: Choose the routing protocol from the list below. The answer starts with O, ends with PF, and is 4 letters long.
leaked_cue: The pattern hint spells out O-S-P-F letter by letter.
clean_version: Choose the routing protocol from the list below.
explanation: A pattern hint reduces the task to decoding a riddle. Once the pattern 'O...PF, 4 letters' is given, only OSPF fits — the learner no longer reasons about routing protocols.

title: Longest option wins
prompt: Pick the right statement about NAT overload. Remember: the longest, most detailed option is the correct one.
leaked_cue: Option length is handed over as the selection strategy.
clean_version: Pick the right statement about NAT overload.
explanation: Length cues let the learner answer without understanding the content — they just compare lengths. The clean version removes the strategy hint so correctness must come from knowledge.

title: The position gives it away
prompt: Select the correct IPv6 address type. The correct choice is the second option.
leaked_cue: The answer's position in the list is revealed.
clean_version: Select the correct IPv6 address type.
explanation: Revealing the position makes the exercise trivially solvable without any IPv6 knowledge. The clean version leaves the learner to identify the address type from the options themselves.

title: The leak hides in the context
prompt: Which protocol runs on port 443 and provides encryption for web traffic? (The one the browser uses with HTTPS.)
leaked_cue: Mentioning port 443 and HTTPS narrows the answer to exactly one protocol.
explanation: Semantic leaks hand over the defining attributes of the answer — port and use case — so the learner only has to match the description. The clean version asks for the same knowledge without pre-answering it.
